headline: Review US Forest Service Site for Black Creek Water Levels
reservation: DeSoto National Forest does not require entry permits for general recreation, but specific developed sites like Big Biloxi require day-use fees paid on-site. Developed campgrounds and specialized trail permits for ATVs must be verified through the official Forest Service reservation portal; changing systems require checking the official site for current availability.

days.title: Tuxachanie Rails and Pine Ridges

stops.name: Tuxachanie Trailhead
stops.detail: Hike the initial miles of this historic trail following an old railroad grade through pine ridges and cypress ponds.

stops.name: Buttercup Flats
stops.detail: Observe rare carnivorous pitcher plants and sundews in these nutrient-poor boggy savannahs.

days.driving: Allow 70–90 minutes; road conditions in rural forest areas vary.
days.note: Trails are relatively flat but sandy; pace yourself against the southern humidity.

days.title: Paddling the National Scenic River

stops.name: Black Creek National Scenic River
stops.detail: Navigate the tannin-stained waters by canoe or kayak past gleaming white sandbars and deep hardwood bottomlands.

stops.name: Black Creek Wilderness
stops.detail: Experience profound isolation in this motorized-vehicle-free zone while watching for river otters and kingfishers.

days.driving: Allow 45–60 minutes for local transfer and shuttle logistics.
days.note: Check for fallen trees or 'strainers' that may require careful navigation after heavy rains.

days.title: Forest Life and Recreation Areas

stops.name: Big Biloxi Recreation Area
stops.detail: Utilize the picnic facilities and easy river access for a relaxed morning of nature study.

stops.name: Bethel Bicycle Trail
stops.detail: Cycle through loops of varying difficulty through the pine woods, noting the unique challenge of sandy soil.

days.driving: Allow 60 minutes for return to airport; conditions vary.
days.note: Verify trail status for mountain bikes as heavy rains lead to temporary maintenance closures.

intel.title: Trailhead Logistics
intel.text: Parking at primary trailheads like Tuxachanie is generally available, but ensure your vehicle is within designated zones to protect forest soil. Avoid blocking service gates used by forest rangers for maintenance.

intel.title: Remote Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is highly inconsistent within the deep pine stands and river valleys of the Black Creek Wilderness. Download offline maps and notify a contact of your route before entering the forest interior.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: Fuel and groceries should be secured in Wiggins or Hattiesburg before entering the forest perimeter. Retail services are non-existent once you leave the main state highways for forest service roads.

intel.title: Seasonal Planning
intel.text: Late autumn through early spring offers the most comfortable temperatures for long-distance hiking. Summer visits should be planned for early morning to avoid peak heat and high insect activity.

intel.title: Specialized Trails
intel.text: Rattlesnake Bay ATV Trail and Big Creek Horse Trail require specific user permits and adhere to seasonal openings. Always verify current status on the official Forest Service website before transporting equipment.

plan.arrival: Upon arrival at Hattiesburg Laurel Regional (PIB), pick up your rental vehicle and stock up on water and supplies in Hattiesburg before the 67-minute drive south to the forest edge.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is suitable for main forest roads, but check rental restrictions for unpaved Forest Service roads; high clearance is beneficial after storms.
plan.goldenHour: Black Creek Sandbars, where the tannin-dark water reflects evening light; seasonal visibility varies by canopy density.
